title: Pollution regulation on plant total factor productivity

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with two-way fixed effects (unit and year).  

Why: The regulation only binds for “high-emission” plants (treated = 1). It starts in period 4 (post = 1). This creates the canonical 2 × 2 DID set-up.

Key assumption: Absent the regulation, log-TFP trends at high- and low-emission plants would have followed parallel paths (Parallel Trends). We will partially probe this with an event-study graph and a pre-period placebo test.

## 2. R Code
```r
# install.packages("fixest")       # uncomment if not installed
# install.packages("did")          # for robustness/event-study
# install.packages("ggplot2")      # plotting

library(fixest)
library(ggplot2)
library(did)    # Callaway-Sant’Anna implementation for robustness

# 1. Read data ------------------------------------------------------------
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s07_data.csv")

# Make sure identifiers are factors for fixed effects
df$unit_id <- factor(df$unit_id)
df$period  <- factor(df$period)

# 2. Baseline DID with two-way FE ----------------------------------------
did_fe <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, 
                data = df, 
                cluster = "unit_id")
cat("\n--- Baseline DID result ---\n")
print(summary(did_fe, cluster = "unit_id")$coeftable)

# 3. Pre-period placebo (fake treatment in period 3) ----------------------
df$placebo_post      <- ifelse(as.numeric(as.character(df$period)) >= 3, 1, 0)
df$placebo_treat_int <- df$treated * df$placebo_post

placebo_fe <- feols(y ~ placebo_treat_int | unit_id + period,
                    data = df[df$period %in% c("1","2","3"), ],  # only pre-periods
                    cluster = "unit_id")
cat("\n--- Placebo DID through period 3 ---\n")
print(summary(placebo_fe, cluster = "unit_id")$coeftable)

# 4. Event-study (dynamic leads/lags) ------------------------------------
df$time_index <- as.numeric(as.character(df$period))
df$rel_time   <- df$time_index - 4       # 0 = first treated year
df$rel_time_f <- factor(df$rel_time)

event_fe <- feols(y ~ i(rel_time_f, treated, ref = "-1") | unit_id + period,
                  data = df, cluster = "unit_id")

# Extract coefficients for plot
event_sum <- broom::tidy(event_fe)
event_sum <- subset(event_sum, grepl("rel_time_f::", term))
event_sum$rel_time <- as.numeric(gsub("i\\(rel_time_f,treated,ref = \"-1\"\\)::","",event_sum$term))

# Plot (saved to file in case console is non-GUI)
p <- ggplot(event_sum, aes(x = rel_time, y = estimate)) +
     geom_point() +
     geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = estimate - 1.96*std.error,
                       ymax = estimate + 1.96*std.error), width = .2) +
     geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
     labs(title = "Event-Study: High- vs Low-Emission Plants",
          x = "Years relative to regulation (t=0 is first treated year)",
          y = "Log-TFP differential") +
     theme_minimal()
ggsave("event_study_plot.png", p, width = 6, height = 4)

# 5. Robustness: Callaway-Sant’Anna DID (heterogeneous timing) -----------
cs_res <- att_gt(yname = "y",
                 tname = "period",
                 idname = "unit_id",
                 gname = "treated",   # group = always-treated vs never
                 data = df,
                 panel = TRUE)
agg_cs <- aggte(cs_res, type = "dynamic")
cat("\n--- Callaway-Sant’Anna aggregated ATT ---\n")
print(agg_cs$aggte)
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: Negative. Tightened air-quality standards likely forced high-emission plants to retrofit capital or curtail output, depressing log-TFP relative to low-emission peers.

Magnitude: A drop of roughly −0.05 to −0.10 log-points (≈ 5–10 %) in the years immediately following the regulation, persisting but tapering in later periods as plants adjust.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID — treated=above-threshold plants, control=below-threshold; shock=tighter regulation
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: High-emission plants experience productivity decline after regulation tightening
